This policy keeps source, generated\nstate, runtime output, fixtures, and historical evidence from competing as if\nthey had the same authority.\n\nThe governing rule:\n\n```text\nEvery tracked file must be source, fixture, policy, reference, intentional\narchive, or an explicitly owned generated/vendored surface. `generated_ignored`   | Reproducible generated output that should not be tracked.                                       | Ignore or remove from git after verification.               |\n| `runtime_state`       | Local state written by tools, runtimes, harnesses, or automations.                              | Do not track unless converted into a documented fixture.    |\n| Do not add\nprocess, artifacts, Linear work, skill routing, evals, or governance because\nserious systems usually have them. analogy_or_template_rejected: \"\"\n  proof_required: \"\"\n  context_load_effect: reduced|neutral|increased|unknown\n  routing_effect: clearer|neutral|worse|unknown\n  decision_type: Type 1|Type 2\n  outcome: proceed|ask|defer|reject|delete_or_collapse\n```\n\n## Decision Rules\n\n- If the reason is \"good systems usually have this\", reject or defer.\n- If the failure is real, repeated, high-risk, or moat-critical, look for the\n  smallest proof-producing mechanism before adding a new surface.\n- If the decision is irreversible, architecture-shaping, closure-sensitive, or\n  expensive to unwind, treat it as Type 1 and require stronger proof.\n- If the decision is reversible, local, low-risk, and easy to validate, treat it\n  as Type 2 and prefer a fast feedback slice.\n- Headless Mode\n\nWhen user input is unavailable, do not ask optional questions. They are not the Harness\nEngineering lifecycle, not a replacement for `.harness` artifacts, and not a\nhidden authority for Linear closure.\n\nUse this contract when a Harness Engineering stage proposes, plans, reviews, or\ndepends on plugin-declared hooks such as `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` `hooks`,\n`hooks/hooks.json`, `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, or `Stop` behavior.\n\n## Load When\n\n- A spec or plan proposes plugin hooks, runtime guardrails, startup context, or\n  lifecycle enforcement inside a plugin.\n- A code review touches plugin manifests, hook declarations, hook commands, or\n  scripts invoked from hooks.\n- An eval or closure recommendation depends on hook behavior.\n- A compound/state reconstruction uses startup context, tool blocking, or stop\n  handoff evidence that may have been produced by plugin hooks.\n\n## Capability Status\n\n- `plugin_hooks` is feature-gated runtime behavior. Treat it as optional unless\n  the active Codex config proves plugins, hooks, `plugin_hooks`, and the target\n  plugin are enabled.\n- HE must preserve a fallback skill, validator, or eval path while\n  `plugin_hooks` can be disabled or unavailable.\n- Plugin hooks may make guardrails more portable, but they must not be the only\n  correctness path for closure, routing, or artifact generation.\n- Plugin hook declarations should prefer the default `hooks/hooks.json`\n  convention unless a custom manifest path or inline config has a concrete\n  reason.\n- Hook commands must use plugin-scoped placeholders such as `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and\n  `${PLUGIN_DATA}` when referencing plugin-owned files. Interfaces\\\\n\\\\n### Packaging Hygiene Interface\\\\n\\\\nThe packaging hygiene check must expose:\\\\n\\\\n```json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"schema_version\\\\\\\": 1,\\\\n  \\\\\\\"root\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"absolute plugin root\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"status\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"pass | fail\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"blocked_paths\\\\\\\": []\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAcceptance depends on `status: pass` for the canonical HE plugin tree, or a\\\\nspecific fail result whose blocked paths are intentionally still present and\\\\ntracked as blockers.\\\\n\\\\n### Eval Report Validator Interface\\\\n\\\\nThe eval report validator must reject closure when a required side-effect\\\\nvalidator is `not-run`.\\\\n\\\\nRequired behavior:\\\\n\\\\n- `Validator Decision: not-run` plus `Blocks Completion: no` is invalid for a\\\\n  protected side-effect action.\\\\n- The validator emits a hard error that says the not-run validator must block\\\\n  completion.\\\\n- The validator/test suite preserves the mixed pass/not-run warning contract\\\\n  when pass statuses coexist with not-run evidence, but the warning cannot\\\\n  downgrade the hard error.\\\\n\\\\n### Release Eval Runner Interface\\\\n\\\\nThe lifecycle release eval runner must classify command-surface failure\\\\nexplicitly and must consume router-sample validation as release-confidence\\\\nevidence when the release profile requires routing proof.\\\\n\\\\nRequired behavior:\\\\n\\\\n- Missing `./bin/ask` or non-executable `./bin/ask` is reported as a degraded\\\\n  environment/recovery condition with an actionable message.\\\\n- A missing command surface does not masquerade as a skill eval pass.\\\\n- Release output distinguishes `skill_failed`, `runner_unavailable`,\\\\n  `runner_timeout`, and `validation_skipped`.\\\\n- The JSON summary exposes enough status for `he-eval-report` to decide whether\\\\n  closure is blocked without parsing stderr.\\\\n\\\\n### Routing Map Sample Interface\\\\n\\\\nRouter sample execution remains owned by\\\\n`Plugins/harness-engineering/scripts/validate_routing_map.py`.\\\\n\\\\nRequired behavior:\\\\n\\\\n- `validate_routing_map.py --run-router-samples --json` fails when a required\\\\n  route sample fails or selects the wrong stage.\\\\n- A skipped router sample is allowed only when the caller did not request\\\\n  sample execution.\\\\n- A release lane that claims router confidence must either run\\\\n  `validate_routing_map.py --run-router-samples --json` or record release\\\\n  confidence as blocked.\\\\n- Optional sample skips may remain warnings only outside release-confidence\\\\n  claims.\\\\n\\\\n### Eval Report Closure Interface\\\\n\\\\n`he-eval-report` must treat this slice as closure-sensitive after\\\\nimplementation.\\\\n\\\\nRequired behavior:\\\\n\\\\n- The eval report cites command output for SA-001 through SA-004.\\\\n- A not-run or skipped required gate maps to `Blocked` or `Needs rework`, not\\\\n  `Complete with follow-up`.\\\\n- Linear completion remains `not_applicable` unless a live Linear issue is\\\\n  created and linked after this spec.\\\\n\\\\n## Invariants\\\\n\\\\n- Missing validation is never proof.\\\\n- Not-run required validators block completion.\\\\n- Release-confidence runners must distinguish environment blockers from skill\\\\n  behavior failures.\\\\n- Required samples cannot be skipped silently.\\\\n- Packaging hygiene is a release input, not cosmetic cleanup.\\\\n- Phase 1 fixes must not create new HE lifecycle stages.\\\\n- Linear remains execution tracking; `.harness` remains cognition and proof.\\\\n\\\\n## Failure And Recovery\\\\n\\\\n| Failure | Required Response | Recovery |\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\n| Packaging hygiene reports blocked paths | Block release confidence | Remove generated clutter or document an explicit blocker with path evidence. |\\\\n| Not-run side-effect validator does not block completion | Block eval-report closure | Fix validator do not claim release pass. |\\\\n| Required router sample execution skipped | Block release confidence | Run the required sample or mark the release lane blocked with reason. |\\\\n| Validation command unavailable | Mark blocked, not pass | Record exact command and concrete missing dependency. |\\\\n| Fix broadens into Next/Later roadmap | Stop implementation | Return to `he-plan` and split Model\\\\n\\\\n```yaml\\\\ndomain_model:\\\\n  status: applicable\\\\n  bounded_context: Harness Engineering lifecycle proof\\\\n  core_domain_relevance: core\\\\n  entities:\\\\n    - name: continue, or hand off.\\\\\\\"\\\\n      lifecycle_states: blocked, needs_rework, complete_with_follow_up, complete\\\\n  value_objects:\\\\n    - name: degraded_mode\\\\n      equality_rule: \\\\\\\"environment unavailability plus explicit recovery action\\\\\\\"\\\\n      immutability_expectation: stable within one eval run\\\\n    - name: required_sample_execution\\\\n      equality_rule: \\\\\\\"router sample marked required by release lane\\\\\\\"\\\\n      immutability_expectation: stable within one release profile\\\\n  aggregates:\\\\n    - name: domain_services:\\\\n    - name: release_eval_runner\\\\n      reason: aggregates skill eval results and classifies release confidence\\\\n    - name: eval_report_validator\\\\n      reason: prevents   - context: he-eval-report\\\\n      translation_rule: closure proof is evaluated after implementation, not inferred from plan completion.\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## Lifecycle\\\\n\\\\nExpected HE Interfaces\\\\n\\\\n### Packaging Hygiene Interface\\\\n\\\\nThe packaging hygiene check must expose:\\\\n\\\\n```json\\\\n{\\\\n  \\\\\\\"schema_version\\\\\\\": 1,\\\\n  \\\\\\\"root\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"absolute plugin root\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"status\\\\\\\": \\\\\\\"pass | fail\\\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\\\"blocked_paths\\\\\\\": []\\\\n}\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nAcceptance depends on `status: pass` for command unavailable | Mark blocked, not pass | Record exact command and concrete missing dependency. |\\\\n| Fix broadens into Next/Later roadmap | Stop implementation | Return to `he-plan` and split
